sorries.obstruction: (iii) Aut(Σ) = {Id} for a cone sphere with ≥ 3 cone points of angle ≠ 2π and pairwise distinct angles (the paper's l.1933 'if all the θ_i are different then Aut(M) = {Id}', through Aut(Σ) ≅ Aut(M)). An automorphism f preserves cone angles (IsConePoint.angle_eq), so it fixes these ≥ 3 cone points, and it is an orientation-preserving isometry of the cone metric. The missing step is a fixed-point theorem for 𝕊²: a non-identity such isometry has finite order (compact isometry group with no circle subgroup, since a circle action on 𝕊² has exactly two fixed points), and a non-identity orientation-preserving periodic homeomorphism of 𝕊² has exactly two fixed points (Brouwer–Kerékjártó, or Lefschetz–Hopf: each fixed point has index +1 and L(f) = 2). Neither the Lefschetz theorem, nor Kerékjártó's theorem, nor the metric of a cone surface is at this mathlib pin or in the library. The obligation is equivalent to this statement (GX.thurstonSuspensionFacts_iff, 0 sorry).

findings: l.1933 ('For instance, if all the θ_i are different then Aut(M)={Id}'): asserted without argument. Through Aut(Σ) ≅ Aut(M) it is the claim Aut(Σ) = {Id}, which is true (each automorphism fixes the ≥ 3 cone points; a non-identity orientation-preserving isometry of a cone sphere has finite order and then exactly two fixed points, Brouwer–Kerékjártó / Lefschetz–Hopf) but rests on a fixed-point theorem for 𝕊². It carries the whole weight of the cex's rigidity: in Lean, GX.ThurstonSuspensionFacts is EQUIVALENT to it (GX.thurstonSuspensionFacts_iff, 0 sorry). A gap in the argument, not a false statement; the author may want a sentence or a citation.

l.1933 ('An automorphism of M has to fix O since singular locus is homeomorphic to a line except at O'): true, and proved for every local isomorphism of open sets containing O (GX.IsConeSphere.thurston_fixes_centre). The argument needs at least three singular rays: near O the singular locus is a star of ≥ 3 arcs, near any other singular point an arc. With two cone points (the football, GX.Spherical.Football) it is an arc through O and the topological argument fails. Troyanov's condition supplies three (TroyanovAngleCondition.three_le_card_ne_two_pi), so the cex stands; the justification is 'a star with ≥ 3 branches at O' rather than 'a line except at O'.

l.1933 ('the natural map Aut(Σ) → Aut(M) is a group isomorphism'): proved (DEC-175 (c), GX.IsConeSphere.thurstonSuspAut_bijective, GX.IsConeSphere.thurstonSuspAutEquiv, 0 sorry), with no distinctness of the angles: it holds for every cone sphere with ≥ 3 cone points of angle ≠ 2π. The same proof gives the local form 'these remarks hold for all neighborhoods of O': a local isomorphism at O is susp(f) near O (GX.IsConeSphere.thurston_eq_susp_near_centre).

l.1935 ('locally we may construct a rotation around any of the axes and since those cannot be extended'): proved with the half-turn of the cone C_θ read in an X_θ-chart and suspended (GX.IsConeSphere.thurston_exists_local_ne_id). Non-extension follows from Aut(M) = {Id} alone (any local isomorphism moving a point is not extendable), so 'generic Σ' enters the cex only through Aut(Σ) = {Id}.
questions: (iii) Aut(Σ) = {Id}, the paper's l.1933 claim (no argument, no citation), is left as a tagged sorry, per DEC-23/26 (cited results are formalized, not assumed). Formalizing it needs a fixed-point theorem for 𝕊² (Kerékjártó's theorem on periodic homeomorphisms, or Lefschetz–Hopf) plus the finiteness of the isometry group, a project of its own. Should it be carried as a named external result (a DEC), or stay an open obligation? Reading taken meanwhile: open obligation, stated as GX.IsConeSphere.singularAut_eq_bot.

OQ-92 (open): the reading taken is l.1930's printed condition for GX.ThurstonSuspensionFacts (unchanged). Evidence for the ruling: the suspension facts need only '≥ 3 angles ≠ 2π', which Theorem C's condition also gives (GX.TroyanovAngleConditionC.three_le_card_ne_two_pi). So the C-form GX.ThurstonSuspensionFactsC follows from the same (iii) (GX.thurstonSuspensionFactsC'), and it implies the printed form. Moving to C does not grow this target's scope beyond (iii) for those tuples.

kb_proposals: Rays over singular points of a Thurston suspension are singular: GX.thurston_mem_reg_of_mk_mem_reg is ConicStructure.mem_reg_of_mk_mem_reg adapted line by line (c.coneChart → (sphConic σ₀).coneChart, (h : G) → liftSO W h, symm_mk_smul → sphConic_symm_smul). The transport of kb 0007 is not needed; that entry's 'Not done yet' can go.

Reading a.e. isomorphisms of open subsets in AMBIENT charts: GX.IsAEMorphism.eventually_smul_eq_of_opens (any charts at a regular point), and its converse GX.isAEMorphism_of_opens_of_eventually. GX.opensOPH turns a homeomorphism of opens into an OpenPartialHomeomorph of the ambient spaces, GX.opensHomeoOf goes back. With them a local construction is checked by chart computations only.

Rotations of the cone C_θ: GX.SphCone.halfRot = orbitsHomeomorph of (rot (1/2), id), an automorphism by isAEMorphismOf_quotientBase with GX.conicalDev_rot. Suspend a local isomorphism F of Σ with GX.thurston_isAEMorphism_posChart (Susp.posChart F).

A local isomorphism of a Thurston suspension fixing the centre is a suspension near O: GX.thurston_reading_fixes_northPole (continuation along rays with the polar profile c(t) = (1−t²)/(1+t²), GX.fst_coneChart, uniqueness by GX.eq_of_inner_eqOn_sphere), GX.exists_liftSO_of_smul_northPole, then GX.thurston_eq_map_near_centre.

Topological rigidity of the centre: a connected subset of the singular rays lies on one ray, because dir maps it into a finite set (GX.IsPreconnected.subsingleton_of_subset_finite); used for GX.IsConeSphere.thurston_fixes_centre.

What remains of cex:start_singular_manifold_homeomorphic beyond Troyanov is exactly Aut(Σ) = {Id} (GX.thurstonSuspensionFacts_iff); it needs a fixed-point theorem for 𝕊² (Kerékjártó / Lefschetz–Hopf), not at this pin.
